definition: The proportion of positive predictions made by a model that are actually correct.
details: Precision is especially important in settings where false positives are costly, such as spam detection or medical diagnosis screening.
story: Picture a scoreboard at a science fair: you need a fair, agreed way to tell who actually won. A fair scoreboard keeps everyone honest. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. A good metric is a ruler that does not bend when you lean on it. And that, done honestly, is Precision.
